Hello from Wenatchee Washington 🏔️🌲❤️
Three beautiful little girls—Paityn, Evelyn, and Olivia—were stolen from us. Bright, radiant, and full of empathy, they reflected their mother’s strength, heart, and spirit. They were everything you’d hope for in a child—compassionate, kind, and deeply connected to those around them. Our community is dimmer without their light.

As a mother and grandmother, I carry this grief like a stone. I want nothing more than to hold Whitney and take even a fraction of her pain away. Her grace in the face of unimaginable loss—the way she spoke about her daughters with such raw honesty and love—was gut-wrenching.

Meanwhile, Travis is hiding in the Enchantments, likely planning to ride it out until winter. But once the snow falls and food runs out, he’ll get desperate. That’s when he’ll surface—breaking into cabins to survive. He’s not quite the Barefoot Bandit, not quite Israel Keyes, but somewhere in between.

When he’s found, justice must be served—for Paityn, Evelyn, and Olivia. They deserve nothing less.

At the very least, there should be accountability if not legal, then moral.

I keep replaying it all in my head, trying to make sense of it. What loophole, what statute, what lapse in judgment allowed for children to be placed in the unsupervised care of an unmedicated father who was clearly battling mental illness? My mind is blown, and my heart aches deeply for the mother and the family for what was lost, and what could have been prevented.

God bless the family and all who are close to them.
